# Same-normal integer-tilt selection: exact structure and an isolated-minimum obstruction

Fix a finite complete integer base `P`, positive convex fibers `K_z` in
`R^d`, a source `(p,y)` with `y in int K_p`, and a UNIT continuous
normal `u`. Let `L=span(P-p)`, and restrict integer tilts to `a in L`.
Write

    v_z=z-p, c_z(a)=u.y-a.v_z,
    G_z(c)=|K_z intersect {u.x>=c}|,
    F(a)=sum_z G_z(c_z(a)).                                (1)

The following results concern minimization over the SAME continuous
normal. A global depth-attaining cap necessarily minimizes (1), but a
minimizer of (1) need not minimize over continuous normals. No claim that
every minimizing tilt pays a prescribed deformation is made.

The precise obstruction is that a minimizing tilt cannot always be moved
to a supporting transition. This fails at a genuine global deepest
source, with all traces proper and with nonlinear section densities.
The example is already implicit in archived radial-simplex results;
the arbitrary-body supporting derivative and rank alternative below
state the interface needed by the proposed selection route.

## 1. Attainment, finite representatives, and the exact ray tail

Choose `H>max_{z,x in K_z}|u.(x-y)|`. For any `a`, keep each evaluation
`a.v_z` inside `[-H,H]` fixed, and impose the corresponding inequality
`b.v_z>=H` or `b.v_z<=-H` on the remaining evaluations. The resulting
nonempty polyhedron contains `a`. Its minimum-norm point `b` belongs to
the span of the active constraint rows: perturbations annihilating all
active rows are feasible in both signs, hence orthogonal to `b`.
Selecting a linearly independent basis of active rows gives

    b=D_I^T(D_I D_I^T)^(-1)t_I,  |t_I|<=sqrt(|I|)H.

There are only finitely many row bases from the fixed vectors `v_z`.
Consequently `|b|<=C(P,p)H`, while every actual fiber trace is unchanged.
Strictness of the support bound `H` preserves full/empty traces as sets,
not merely up to measure zero. With no active rows, `b=0`.

Thus every value of `F` is represented in one compact ball. Nonvertical
hyperplane boundaries have zero `d`-volume in every positive fiber, so
dominated convergence makes `F` continuous, and its infimum is attained.
This is the archived bounded-tilt lemma from
`candidate 65cb1818e941a654`,
specialized here to fixed `u`; it is not a new compactness theorem.

For every nonzero ray direction `h in L`, there is a finite `T` such
that for ALL `t>=T`,

    F(a+th)=sum_{h.v_z>0}|K_z|
               +sum_{h.v_z=0} G_z(c_z(a)).                  (2)

Every nonzero-drift fiber has saturated by that finite time; zero-drift
traces remain exactly fixed. Reversing `h` gives the other tail. In
particular `F` is not coercive, even when its minimizer is unique.
The zero-drift terms in (2) are actual continuous cuts, not whole-fiber
boundary mass of a purely integer halfspace. These two notions must not
be identified.

## 2. Exact first-order structure, including supporting facets

Let

    l_z=min_{K_z}u.x, r_z=max_{K_z}u.x,
    w_z(s)=H^(d-1)(K_z intersect {u.x=s}) for l_z<=s<=r_z.

For `d>=2`, `w_z` is continuous and positive in the open support interval;
its root of order `d-1` is concave. Its one-sided endpoint limits equal
the measures of the actual exposed faces. For the latter statement,
contracting the exposed face toward an interior point supplies the
lower limit, and convergence into arbitrarily small neighborhoods of
the compact face supplies the upper limit. For `d=1`, the interior
density and both endpoint counting measures are one.

At a fixed tilt `a`, partition fibers into proper cuts `I`, empty-side
support contacts `E` with `c_z=r_z`, full-side support contacts `B` with
`c_z=l_z`, and the strictly saturated fibers. Set

    g=sum_{z in I}w_z(c_z)v_z,
    A=sum_{z in E}[0,w_z(r_z)v_z],
    Bcal=sum_{z in B}[0,w_z(l_z)v_z].                       (3)

The sums of segments are actual finite zonotopes in tilt space. A
zero-area supporting face contributes a zero segment. For a tilt
velocity `h`, put `b_z=h.v_z`. Direct integration of the one-dimensional
section densities gives the exact right derivative

    F'(a;h)=g.h +sum_E w_z(r_z)(b_z)_+
                    +sum_B w_z(l_z)min(b_z,0)
            =h_{g+A}(h)-h_{-Bcal}(h).                     (4)

The signs reflect actual closed-cap statuses. Lowering an empty-side
support threshold creates volume, while raising a full-side support
threshold removes volume. A supporting facet is not assigned arbitrary
inside or outside mass. Strictly saturated fibers contribute zero.

Consequently absence of a strict first-order decreasing tilt is
EQUIVALENT to the concrete inclusion

    -Bcal subset g+A.                                      (5)

This follows from the elementary support-function characterization of
compact convex-set inclusion. In particular every local minimizer
satisfies (5). Its allocation order is explicit: EVERY point of the
negative full-support zonotope must be representable using the SAME
proper gradient plus some empty-support allocation. Merely finding one
balancing allocation is weaker and is not substituted for (5).

If (4) is strictly positive on the unit sphere of `L`, the tilt is a
strict isolated local minimum. Indeed the section-density integral
expansions have error `o(|h|)` uniformly as `h->0`, since only finitely
many scalar profiles occur. Compactness then gives a uniform positive
linear margin. At equality directions, (5) alone is only a necessary
first-order condition and says nothing about second-order payment.

This is a fixed-normal specialization of the archived supporting-branch
allocation calculus, not a new universal stress or Gamma inequality.
Its utility is that it distinguishes the support-transition choice
from the smooth proper-tilt alternatives without a minimax swap.

## 3. A support-transition versus full-rank section alternative

Suppose `a` is a global minimizer and no fiber threshold is at a support
endpoint. If the proper-base vectors `{v_z:z in I}` fail to span `L`,
choose nonzero `h in L` annihilating them. All proper traces remain
EXACTLY fixed on the line `a+th`. All other traces remain saturated
until their first support transition. Some saturated fiber has
`h.v_z!=0`, since all base vectors span `L`. In one of the two directions
that fiber must leave its current saturated status at a finite time.
Choose the first such transition among all fibers. Up to and including
that time, continuity shows that `F` remains constant and globally
minimal. Thus a minimizing tilt at an ACTUAL supporting transition is
available.

It follows that one can select a minimizing tilt which either has a
support transition or has proper-base span equal to `L`. At a
support-free minimizer, differentiation of (1) gives `g=0`. In the
full-rank alternative, the positive weights of the NON-OWN proper
sections therefore give the actual anchored relation

    p=sum_{z!=p, z in I} lambda_z z,
    lambda_z=w_z(c_z)/sum_{j!=p,j in I}w_j(c_j)>0.           (6)

Its support affinely spans `p+L`, and `p` lies in its relative interior.
Decomposing this coefficient vector in its anchored-representation
polytope gives extreme nonself representations supported on the same
proper fibers; their union spans `L`. One cannot in general replace
that union by a SINGLE full-dimensional simplex relation: even the
center of a square can have only opposite-pair extreme representations.

Relation (6) is a section-area balance. It does not assert equality in
the corresponding whole-fiber Minkowski inclusion or a tight support
contact. That missing geometric assertion cannot be obtained from
integer-tilt stationarity alone.

## 4. Proper-section second variation without a C2 assumption

At a support-free tilt, proper thresholds lie in the interiors of their
section supports. For `d>=2` concavity of `w_z^(1/(d-1))` supplies finite
one-sided derivatives `w'_{z,-},w'_{z,+}` there; the positive power
preserves existence of these derivatives. For `b_z=h.v_z`, direct
integration gives

    F(a+th)=F(a)+t g.h +(t^2/2)Q_a(h)+o(t^2), t down to0,

    Q_a(h)=-sum_{z in I, b_z>0} b_z^2 w'_{z,-}(c_z)
           -sum_{z in I, b_z<0} b_z^2 w'_{z,+}(c_z).        (7)

Terms with `b_z=0` vanish. At a local minimum `g=0` and `Q_a(h)>=0`
for every `h`. If every proper density is differentiable at its cut,
this becomes the archived integer-normal Hessian condition

    -sum_{z in I} w'_z(c_z)v_z v_z^T >=0.                  (8)

When a proper section itself is at a density kink, (7), rather than one
arbitrarily selected Hessian, is the exact one-sided test. In dimension
one all proper densities are constant, so `F` is affine on each strict
trace cell. A support-free minimum then has zero gradient and can move
unchanged to a support transition whenever `L` is nonzero. The next
example shows that this interval behavior does not extend to `d>=2`.

## 5. Genuine globally critical isolated minima with nonlinear slices

For `d>=2` use the centered simplex

    T_d={x_j>=-1, sum_j x_j<=1},
    V_d=(d+1)^d/d!, Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d,

and the ACTUAL product with complete base `P={-1,0,1}`. Its source is
`Y=(0,0)`. Fix `u=e_1`; its section density is

    w(s)=(d-s)^(d-1)/(d-1)! for -1<s<d.                    (9)

Thus for `d>=3` the section density itself is nonlinear. The single-
fiber upper cap is

    G(c)=V_d for c<=-1;
         (d-c)^d/d! for -1<=c<=d;
         0 for c>=d.

The fixed-normal tilt objective is

    F(a)=Gamma_d V_d+G(a)+G(-a).

For `|a|<=1`, all traces are proper except possible supporting equality
at the two endpoints, and

    F(a)=[d^d+(d+a)^d+(d-a)^d]/d!.

Strict convexity of `s^d` on positive arguments gives
`F(a)>F(0)=3 Gamma_d V_d` for every nonzero `|a|<=1`. If `|a|>=1`,
one endpoint trace is full, so

    F(a)>=Gamma_d V_d+V_d>3 Gamma_d V_d.                   (10)

The last inequality follows from `2 Gamma_d<1` for `d>=2`. Hence
`a=0` is the UNIQUE global minimizing tilt, all three traces are proper,
and every supporting-transition tilt has a strictly larger cap mass.
The integer-normal Hessian there is

    F''(0)=2d^(d-2)/(d-2)!>0.                              (11)

For example `d=3` gives the nonlinear density `(3-s)^2/2` and
`F(a)=27/2+3a^2` on `|a|<=1`; `d=4` gives
`F(a)=32+8a^2+a^4/12` there. These are positive-volume nonlinear
examples, not discrete interval profiles or formal slice data.

These are also genuinely global critical caps, not just fixed-normal
minima at an arbitrary source. The archived paired-centroid-tail theorem
`candidate 732b11a769399016` gives at least
`2 Gamma_d V_d` from the two reflected endpoint fibers for every
continuous normal and integer tilt; ordinary Grünbaum supplies
`Gamma_d V_d` from the own fiber. Pure integer caps have still larger
closed mass. The `d+1` canonical cylinders attain this bound and cover
every fiber plane, proving the actual global maximum
`Q=3 Gamma_d V_d`. This is the baseline theorem already audited in
`candidate 4e12bc9cd7731df3`.
Every canonical cut is proper on every fiber and has the required full
mixed section centroid. Thus global deepestness and regular criticality
do not remove the isolated-minimum obstruction.

More generally any centrally symmetric finite complete base containing
zero, with the same simplex fiber everywhere, has a UNIQUE minimizing
canonical tilt modulo invisible directions. Pair `z` with `-z` in the
calculation above. Every nonzero tilt in `span(P)` moves some pair and
strictly increases its mass; its local Hessian is the positive matrix

    [d^(d-2)/(d-2)!] sum_z z z^T

on that span. The same archived paired-tail argument proves genuine
global criticality of its untilted canonical cylinders.

## 6. Quantitative stability and the exact limitation of tilt selection

In the three-fiber example, for `0<eta<=1` and every `|a|>=eta`, the
binomial expansion and (10) give

    F(a)-F(0)>=g_eta,
    g_eta=min{[d^(d-2)/(d-2)!]eta^2,
                         (1-2 Gamma_d)V_d}>0.              (12)

For other fibers `L_z` at the same bases, retain the same source and
continuous normal, and let `Delta=sum_z |L_z symmetric_difference T_d|`.
Uniformly over ALL tilts their cap objective differs from `F` by at
most `Delta`. If `2Delta<g_eta`, every global minimizing tilt for that
new fixed-normal objective lies in `(-eta,eta)`. If the bodies are also
sufficiently Hausdorff-close and `eta<1`, all those cuts are proper.
This conclusion includes curved perturbations; it does not assert that
the old source remains globally deepest after an arbitrary perturbation.

Thus pushing a critical integer tilt to a saturation face is justified
by the rank-deficient flat alternative in Section 3, or by additional
special slice structure, but not in general. On an isolated branch any
improving menu selection must change something else: the continuous
normal, the source, or the actual body variation. The exact fixed-cover
payment condition and its supporting allocations remain separate from
the minimization of (1). No arbitrary-body OC or universal paying
tilt-selection theorem is concluded.
